findings.evidence: Tick cadence is now integrated, bounded, and one decision is reused per goal tick, but a live interval change between throttled values retains cooldownRemaining from the old interval. For example, after interval 20 arms cooldown 19, reloading interval 2 still skips up to 19 ticks; changing 2 to 20 can allow again after the old one-tick cooldown. PerformanceSettings also publishes enabled and interval through separate volatile writes and the mixins read them separately, so the AI tuple is not an atomic snapshot.
findings.recommended_fix: Publish the AI enabled/interval tuple atomically without per-tick allocation, read it once at tick HEAD, and have AiMoveCadence detect an effective setting change. On a throttled interval change, deterministically rearm so the next eligible request runs immediately and starts the new interval; document that reload rule.
required_tests: State-machine test changing 20 to 2 and 2 to 20 during cooldown, asserting immediate deterministic rearm and subsequent spacing by the new interval.
Forge Reloading integration test proving one coherent enabled/interval tuple is observed on the next goal tick.

findings.evidence: These active recurring handlers still call PerformanceConfig.EGG_HATCH_CHECK_INTERVAL_TICKS.get() and SHOCK_PARTICLE_INTERVAL_TICKS.get() at lines 18 and 22. findings.recommended_fix: Return PerformanceSettings.eggHatchCheckIntervalTicks() and shockParticleIntervalTicks() from the respective handlers. Confine all ForgeConfigSpec.get() calls to the spec-matched load/reload handler.
